name: Deal ticket and transport contract set-up
definition: Creating, extending or replacing deal tickets and transport contracts in Sitara so that gas at a meter or on a pipeline has a valid deal for the month.

row.name: Deal ticket and transport contract set-up
row.tier_words: seen steadily: 40 or more times over 6 or more months by 3 or more staff

synthesis.description: A round usually starts when a scheduler, volume analyst or accountant finds gas flowing at a meter or on a pipeline with no valid deal: a ticket expired, ended mid-month or was never created. They email the desk, mostly Daren Farmer, asking for a Sitara deal to be created, extended, zeroed out or corrected. The desk or a logistics coordinator enters or extends the ticket and replies with the deal or track number. The requester then checks that the ticket reflects the flow, so that allocations and the Unify volume drafts can clear.
steps: A scheduler or analyst finds flow at a meter with no deal, an expired ticket or an allocation exception.
They email the desk with the meter, dates, counterparty and any existing deal number.
The desk checks Sitara to see whether the existing deal should be extended or a new one created.
The trader or coordinator creates, extends, zeroes or corrects the ticket in Sitara.
The deal or track number is sent back to the requester.
The requester confirms the ticket is released and flows into Unify so allocations and volume drafts can clear.
synthesis.approach: A daily exception report comparing measured flow and allocation exceptions by meter against active Sitara tickets would flag meters with flow but no deal, and tickets expiring before month end, before anyone has to email. A standard request form would capture meter, dates, counterparty, price and existing deal number, and route to the named owner for that pipeline, with the new deal number returned automatically.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are the same request missing the same fields (meter, dates, deal number, extend or create), and many stall on who handles it. A structured request form with a routing owner column removes the back-and-forth and the incorrect terms, while the trader still decides whether to extend or create.

document.markdown:
# Deal ticket and transport contract set-up: template

Draft prepared from 255 emails about this process, for the process owner to review. Evidence about this process, quoted exactly from the emails, is listed at the end.

## Purpose

Use this request form when gas is flowing at a meter or on a pipeline and there is no valid Sitara deal for the month: a ticket expired, ended mid-month, was never created, or is not released. One complete request gives the desk everything it needs to create, extend, zero out or correct the ticket and to send back the deal or track number, so allocations and the Unify volume drafts can clear.

## Who fills it in

People doing this work (counted from the emails): Aimee Lannou (21 written, 5 forwarded), Jackie Young (24 written, 2 forwarded), Michael Olsen (10 written, 3 forwarded), Julie Meyers (8 written, 1 forwarded). Named as owner in the emails: Daren J Farmer (Jun 2001), Danny Conner (Oct 2000), Robert E Lloyd (Jan 2000); the process owner settles which. Owner: [process owner to confirm].

The requester fills it in: the scheduler, volume analyst or accountant who found the meter or pipeline with no valid deal, an expired ticket or an allocation exception. The requester owns the request until the ticket is confirmed released and flowing into Unify.

The desk (the trader or logistics coordinator) fills in the last block, "Desk response", and decides whether to extend or create. The owner for the pipeline, listed in the routing table at [location of routing table], is the person who receives the request. Set up that routing table first and keep it current, with one row per pipeline or meter group and one named owner each, so requests are not passed between people.

## When

- Send a form as soon as flow is found with no deal, an expired ticket, an allocation exception that needs a deal extended, or a deal that is still not released.
- Send one form per meter or pipeline. List several deal numbers on one form only when they are the same change for the same counterparty.
- If there is no reply [proposed: by the end of the same day], send one reminder to the same owner, then escalate to the desk lead [name or role].
- Check the effective date and price against the source before sending. Wrong terms in the first request mean a second request.

## Template

### Request

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Request date | [date] |
| Requester (name and role) | [requester] |
| Action needed | [create / extend / zero out all activity / correct / release] |
| Pipeline | [pipeline] |
| Meter number | [meter number] |
| Counterparty | [counterparty] |
| Existing Sitara deal number(s) | [deal number, or "none"] |
| Effective date from | [date] |
| Effective date to | [date, or end of month] |
| Price | [price and unit] |
| Flow volume | [volume] [unit, for example MMBtu/d] |
| Purchase or sale | [purchase / sale] |
| Reason | [no deal / expired ticket / ended mid-month / allocation exception / not released / wrong terms] |
| Allocation exception or Unify draft blocked | [yes or no, and which] |
| Routed to (owner for this pipeline) | [owner from the routing table] |
| Needed by | [deadline] |

### Desk response

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Existing deal checked in Sitara | [yes / no, deal number found] |
| Decision | [extended existing deal / created new deal / zeroed / corrected] |
| Deal or track number | [number] |
| Date entered | [date] |
| Notes for the requester | [notes] |

### Requester confirmation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Ticket shows as released in Sitara | [yes / no] |
| Ticket reflects the flow | [yes / no] |
| Deal reached Unify, volume draft and allocations clear | [yes / no] |
| Date confirmed | [date] |

## Where it goes

- Send the request by email to the owner named for the pipeline in the routing table, with the desk copied. Put the meter number and action in the subject line, for example "[action]\: meter [meter number], [pipeline]".
- The desk enters or changes the ticket in Sitara and replies on the same thread with the deal or track number.
- The requester checks Sitara and Unify, fills in the confirmation block and replies on the same thread. Keep the thread as the record of the change.
- If the ticket is still not released after the desk reply, say so on the same thread and name the deal number. If the owner is unclear or the request is redirected, copy the desk lead and ask for the owner to be added to the routing table.
- If terms in the form turn out to be wrong (effective date or price), send a corrected form on the same thread and mark it "corrected".
- If the person named for a pipeline is disputed (different people have been given as the one who enters these deals) [confirm still in force], the desk lead decides and updates the routing table.
- Where the accounting arrangements for a new deal must be set up, name the group or person responsible on the form's notes line; volume management as a group and individual colleagues have both been named for this, so confirm which one before sending.
